summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with dizziness and hypotension, initially attributed to recent diarrhea and low baseline blood pressure. He reported right knee pain, and examination revealed a swollen, tender knee. Arthrocentesis showed hemarthrosis with no infection. Blood cultures grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, suggesting a dialysis line infection. He was started on vancomycin, and after two negative cultures, underwent a tunneled dialysis line exchange over wire. The old catheter tip culture confirmed gram-positive cocci. His knee pain improved with fluid removal and analgesia, and he had no signs of endocarditis on echocardiogram. He completed scheduled dialysis, remained afebrile, and was discharged to extended care with a two-week course of vancomycin during dialysis and instructions to monitor the line site and weight.
